title: South Africa’s electricity crises have left productive scars. Its green transition must confront them
summary: Years of power cuts left productive scars: lost manufacturing capacity, investment, export capability and learning that persist after supply improves. A green transition that ignores them may deliver cleaner electricity while reproducing industrial weakness.
keyPoints: Outages reduced investment, employment and exports, mainly among electricity-intensive manufacturers.
Reliable power alone will not bring investment back.
Energy reform must become productive reconstruction.
